purpose: analysis-only linear closed-loop noise model; no loop is run; no scientific claim by itself
configuration: ci derivation of scripts/detector_level_convergence_study.py (eso_scao_smoke_5m_software@2 geometry with det_emccd_12m_medium_derived@3 physics), m_AB 9
mask_rule: the reconstructor is probed with exactly the rows that carry noise valid (one fixed mask per rule for L, the injection and Sigma); the primary rule takes the operator the loop used in the plurality of analysed frames; the series' all-valid propagation weights are kept for the first draft's scalar value

noise_covariance.source: sidecar_realized_residuals (c_noisy - c_expected on the noisy arm's lenslets, ddof 1, 2x2 per lenslet)
noise_covariance.label: m9

operator.definition: the row set the noisy arm's reconstructor used in the plurality of analysed frames (<arm>__measurement_row_masks); the model's operator R is probed on exactly this set; whether the fixed operator describes the run is decided by the error bounds in prediction.operator_bounds, not by these fractions
operator.sigma_frames: frames in which the noisy arm used the modal operator

burn_in.definition: burn-in frames the linear model does not carry into the analysed window: a frame with gate activity (a row on which the two arms' masks differ, a rejected reconstruction in either arm, or a recovery action, which the counters give only run-wide and then mark every burn-in frame) or with command saturation above 1e-3 in either arm; a burn-in without such a frame is quiet and carries the modelled state

bracket.definition: rows outside the modal mask whose lenslet has fewer than 10 usable analysed frames carry no covariance of their own; the transient with the actual operators is propagated with their covariance at zero and at the envelope (the largest realized per-axis variance among the lenslets with at least 10 usable frames, cross terms zero), and the operator error is the worse of the two

effective.definition: rows of the modal effective mask (the operator the loop used); covariance over the frames in which the noisy arm used that operator

available.definition: lenslets valid, supported and finite in at least 0.9 of the analysed frames; covariance over each lenslet's own valid frames

strict.definition: lenslets valid, supported and finite in every analysed frame (the E0 rule); covariance over all analysed frames

sidecar_validation.structural: passed (declared table against the runner's canonical units, axes, meanings, dtypes and axis-implied shapes; frame domains; two-arm layout; canonical rows; label)

memory.note: the inventory counts the arrays the tool itself holds (the Lyapunov and propagation working sets as size estimates); the system build's own arrays, the interpreter and the libraries are in the peak resident set only; the dense pupil response is freed once the Gram matrix is formed

feedback_spectrum.definition: eigenvalues of L = R_mask M on the controlled actuators (1 = unit feedback; below 1 = damped mode; the scalar model assumes all 1)
feedback_spectrum.unsensed_modes_note: a mode with feedback below 1e-6 is left unsensed by this mask; with no leak it has a unit pole, no stationary limit exists and the finite-window prediction (the primary quantity) grows with the run length; the count is reported and no rule attaches to it

prediction.units: m2 (piston-removed pupil mean square of the noise-driven correction difference; the sidecar's delta_v_m2 in expectation)
prediction.primary: delta_v_exact_window_m2 (transient from identical initial commands with the noise entering after the latency, averaged over the analysed frames; noise covariance rule 'effective')

operator_bounds.rule: operator-consistent when the operator error, at the worse end of the covariance bracket, is within --operator-tolerance; mask-variable when it is not; not assessable when the time-varying prediction cannot be computed, the bracket is wider than the tolerance, or the carried-state bound cannot be measured; the carried-state bound (gamma over the sensed states when the operator injects nothing into its unsensed modes, over all states otherwise) is a systematic of the comparison, not a threshold

time_varying.definition: the transient propagated with the noisy arm's actual operator of every frame of the run (burn-in included; the increment released at update k carries the operator of frame k - d; each distinct effective mask probed once; Sigma restricted to each operator's rows, the modal rows keeping the effective rule's blocks, rows outside them their own estimate or the bracket); the relative difference from the modal-operator prediction is the operator error, taken at the worse end of the covariance bracket and split into the part carried in from burn-in (actual operators before the window, the modal one inside it) and the part from operator changes inside the window

carried_state.definition: the window mean is affine in the loop's state at the first analysed frame, so a deviation of that state from the modelled one changes the window mean by at most gamma times its change of the first 25-frame block mean, gamma being the largest generalized eigenvalue of the window-mean and first-block-mean quadratic forms; the first-block change is measured as the first analysed block's measured delta_v_m2 mean minus the model's own first-block mean (the per-frame modal transient), with the run's 25-frame block scatter as its uncertainty; bound = gamma_used * (|excess_1| + 2 s_block) / primary, with gamma_used the eigenvalue over the states the operator senses when the operator injects nothing into its unsensed modes (unsensed_mode_injection at or below max_unsensed_injection: a Tikhonov-type reconstructor's left null vectors of L are left null vectors of R, so those modes hold no noise-driven state in the model or in the loop without a flagged event), and the eigenvalue over every state otherwise; the bound over every state is reported as a sensitivity in either case
carried_state.gamma_basis: all states (the operator injects into its weakly sensed modes)

systematic.definition: the model's systematic error budget of this run's prediction, relative: the operator error (worse end of the bracket) plus the carried-state bound; PROTOCOL.md 1.7 subtracts the mean budget of the admissible seeds from the equivalence band

restart_sensitivities.definition: restarts of the modal-operator window from a zero state (identical commands, an empty queue): the share of the primary value carried in from before the window (first analysed frame), from before the last burn-in frame with gate activity or saturation, and the window value under a stationary carried state; sensitivities of the modelled state, not bounds on an unknown one

stationarity.note: a mode the mask leaves unsensed has a unit pole (no leak): no stationary covariance; the finite-window prediction is the primary quantity

comparison.status: mask-variable: operator error +3.86 % exceeds the 2 % tolerance; the prediction is reported and the comparison is descriptive

systematic_budget.definition: the model's systematic error budget of this run's prediction, relative: the operator error (worse end of the bracket) plus the carried-state bound; PROTOCOL.md 1.7 subtracts the mean budget of the admissible seeds from the equivalence band

comparison.note: a pilot-level consistency check of the model against one run; the protocol's acceptance rules, not this ratio, decide anything; a run that is not operator-consistent (mask-variable or not assessable) has a descriptive comparison; the systematic budget enters the closure test of PROTOCOL.md 1.7
